name: 1811 Prairie Avenue — the Miner T. Ames (Coleman) house, Cobb & Frost's rock-faced stone front from the 1888 Inland Architect plate, K01 frontage assembly

grade.why: Pictured: 4 of the pictures on the Images tab show it.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The front block's rear north corner: the draft's frame point u 18.40, v -2.10 (draft position note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 12.250, v -4.000 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the georeference's independent check is 1.47 m RMS. Rotation 179.444 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.) Moved by T-2541 from the corner of the draft's fitted rectangle to the corner of the sheet's own plan: the front block's north wall is the trace's at v -2.1, its rear the line where the trace's north wall steps in, 7.57 m behind the entrance block's stone face.
placement.symbolic_location: 1811 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1811 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).

footprint.note: The front block read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1811-b1) in the lot frame: the entrance block's stone face 7.57 m in front of the line where the trace's north wall steps in from v -2.1 to v -0.1 (18.4 m from the trace's rear), so 7.57 m deep; 10.4 m along the front from the north wall to the south wall's straight line, the trace's own width. The bay's 1.0 m and the stair stand in front of it; the rear range is in rear_wings.

stories.note: '3B; section 2B' on the 1911 sheet: three storeys over a basement, with a two-storey section. T-2542: the 1888 plate shows the third storey of the street front IN THE ROOF, lit by the stone gable over the north bay, with the street slope coming down to about 8.5-8.8 m between the bay and the oriel; K01 counts the storeys under its eave, so two here and the third in the roof, lit by the wall gable (`dormer`). The brick range behind keeps its three walled storeys, which the plate's south flank shows as three rows of windows.

construction.note: The sheet's 'brick with stone front'; the plate shows the rock-faced stone street front and the brick south flank behind it.

principal_floor_m.note: Nine risers of 0.15 m, the stair's count on the plate, so 1.35 m; bounded by the bay's ground-floor sills at 2.0 m over grade, read through the T-2541 camera on the 1888 plate (data/reference_views/coleman_ames_house_1811_prairie/inland_architect_plate.json), and low enough that the door's head clears the oriel's three corbel courses.

storey_heights_m.note: Read through the T-2541 camera on the 1888 plate (data/reference_views/coleman_ames_house_1811_prairie/inland_architect_plate.json): the bay's ground-floor heads at 4.3 m and its first-floor sills at 5.5 m put the second floor near 5.0 m, 3.65 m over the 1.35 m principal floor; the first-floor heads at 7.6 m and the bay's cornice at 8.3 m put the roof storey's floor near 8.4 m. T-2542: the plate's street slope comes down behind the bay and the oriel to about 8.8 m at the front wall's plane (x 290-340 px), so the third storey stands in the roof, not under T-2541's 11.7 m eave. K01's eave is the datum where the roof's plane meets the wall's face, over its 0.35 m eave: 4.14 m over the second floor, at 9.14 m, puts the eave's fascia top at 8.50 m and the soffit, the moulded stone cornice's top, at 8.30 m, the plate's bay cornice. The second storey's wall is carried up as the roof storey's knee wall.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A rock-faced stone front on a brick backing: the K01 contract's thickest masonry front.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A brick side wall of three storeys: the district's K03 default.

service_wall_brick.note: The south flank is brick on the plate and on the 1911 sheet; its colour and bond are not shown (a monochrome print), so the district's common brick.

stone_front.note: The plate's front is rock-faced ashlar in large courses with dressed trim; the T-1837 register reads it brown sandstone (frontage-28-050). The colour is the register's, not the plate's. The smooth ashlar of the bay's upper stage is T-2542's.

street_front_trim.note: The plate's windows are square-headed in plain stone surrounds; their carved heads and the transoms are the finishing ticket's (T-1892).

wall_head.note: A moulded stone cornice at the main eave, where the plate shows the roofs springing from a stone course; its section is the K10 kit's.

roof_form.note: A ridge along the street front, its street slope rising steeply from the eave behind the bay's stone gable and the oriel's pyramid (T-2542), and the front block's side walls carried up in brick as coped gable ends, the south one to the tall stack, as the plate and the Chicagology print show it; the north end, unseen, the same.

roof_pitch_deg.note: T-2542: read through the T-2541 camera on the 1888 plate (data/reference_views/coleman_ames_house_1811_prairie/inland_architect_plate.json): the street slope rises from its eave, at about 8.5-8.8 m, to the roof's apex, x 320 y 240 px, about 16 m over grade if it stands on the ridge 3.78 m behind the front (the ridge's depth is reconstructed; the plate sees no ridge end). 61.2 degrees from the 9.14 m eave datum over 3.78 m rises 6.87 m, to 16.01 m: in the K01 contract's steep band, which a gable read off a source may take. The rear slope falls at about the same pitch to the same wall head.

eave_overhang_m.note: 0.35 m: enough eave for K10's moulded stone cornice (0.32 m proud) under the slate; the plate shows a stone eave course, not a deep soffit. T-2542 trimmed it from 0.4 m so the oriel, 0.5 m out, stands 0.15 m past the eave it is carried through.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: A landing at the door's sill inside the arch.

stoop_width_m.note: The broad stair between its cheek walls, about 2.7 m over the cheeks on the plate through the T-2541 camera on the 1888 plate (data/reference_views/coleman_ames_house_1811_prairie/inland_architect_plate.json), so about 2.2 m of tread.

entrance_bay.note: The door is in the south part of the front, under the deep round arch (the plate). K01 names its ends in the footprint frame, whose v runs south on this side of the avenue, so its 'north' end is the street's south end.

front_bays.note: Centres along the front from its north end (v 0): 0.9 m, the narrow strip north of the bay that the plate shows as a canted face with one narrow window a storey; 3.6 m, behind the bay, whose own windows are the bay's; 7.9 m, the entrance arch's centre, read through the T-2541 camera on the 1888 plate (data/reference_views/coleman_ames_house_1811_prairie/inland_architect_plate.json) at x 400 px.

windows.why_not_ordinary: a basement light under each of the bay's windows, read off the 1888 plate: about 0.95 m across and 1.0 m high, its head at the plate's 1.2 m, flat-headed under a rock-faced course and filled with a scrolled iron grille (T-2916)
the oriel's three tall narrow transomed lights, read off the 1888 plate at about 0.5 m each between stone mullions over a 2.8 m front

bays.note: Read off the plate through the T-2541 camera on the 1888 plate (data/reference_views/coleman_ames_house_1811_prairie/inland_architect_plate.json). NORTH BAY: the front block's north part stands forward of the entrance block (the sheet's stone part p1 draws it about 1.0 m proud); its front, x 112-287 px, is about 3.7 m wide at the bay's own scale (47.4 px/m), with two windows a storey at about 0.3 and 0.78 of its front, iron-grilled basement lights under them, and a cornice at about 8.3 m over which the third storey stands back behind a pierced stone balcony. Built as K08's square-cornered full-height projection, two storeys from grade to 8.4 m: the plate shows (and the sheet draws) its north face CANTED, which K08 has no shape for; that and the bay's smooth upper stage are open on the match record. T-2916: the bay is three storeys of K08, a 1.75 m basement storey under the 3.25 m ground storey and the 2.944 m first, so the string course at 1.67-1.83 m stands where the plate's smooth sill course does (about 1.6-1.9 m, under the ground-floor sills at 2.05 m, unchanged); in it a basement light under each window, 0.95 m across and 1.0 m high from 0.22 m, the plate's lights at x 139-184 and 235-272 px and y 765-819 px (about 1.2 m down to just over grade: the head is the plate's, the sill stands 0.16 m higher because K06's sill stone, 0.1 m deep under the light, must stand on the plinth, not in its face), each barred in K08's grille (five bars and a ring: the plate's grilles are scrolled panels, which the kit draws as bars and one scroll); the bay's plinth is 0.1 m (the kit's 0.6 m would cover the lights' lower half, and the plate's rock-faced courses run down to the walk). On the bay's flat deck a stone balustrade round its cheeks and front (K08's balcony in the bay's stone, T-2780/T-2888): 0.7 m high, the plate's panel and coping at y 392-425 px, 0.3 m posts at the corners as the plate's piers are, a 0.22 m coping, and close-set stone bars at 0.12 m where the plate's panels are pierced fretwork (its interlace is not carved; the bars carry the panel's pierced light and shade). ORIEL: over the entrance arch, corbelled out from about 5.2 m, its front x 340-465 px (about 2.8 m) with three tall transomed lights and a window in each return, its cornice at about 9.1 m; built as K08's corbelled oriel 0.5 m out on three corbel courses from 4.4 m, its returns canted 0.2 m (the plate's are square, and stand further out: K08's oversail rule holds three courses to 0.52 m, and a fourth would bring the corbel down onto the arch). T-2542: carried through the street eave as 1623's is (T-2778), so the eave and the moulded stone cornice die into its cants, under its steep pyramid and finial on K08's spire: its wall top 9.46 m (one 4.46 m storey from 5.0 m), 0.4 m over the plate's cornice at 9.06 m because K01 carries an oriel through the eave only 0.3 m past the eave datum (9.14 m), and its spire rising 2.1 m toward the plate's apex at about 12.0 m. The bay's wall top is the stone cornice's foot (7.94 m), the cornice carried round it to 8.30 m, the plate's 8.3 m.

side_bays.note: The north wall (K01's 'south'): not seen on any picture; two windows a storey, reconstructed.

north_bays.note: The front block's south wall (K01's 'north'), seen on the plate behind the entrance block's stone return: one window a storey, reconstructed at the plate's spacing.

rear_bays.note: The front block's rear wall is covered by the rear range across all but its north 2.0 m.

rear_wings.note: The sheet's main part behind the front block, 8.4 m wide on the south wall's straight line (trace s28fp-1811-b1 p2, v 2.0-10.4 here), drawn as one part to its rear wall 18.4 m back with a drawn division about 4.3 m from the rear: the three-storey range ('3B') and the two-storey rear section ('section 2B'). The plate and the Chicagology print show the range's south flank in brick, three rows of windows over a basement, evenly spaced, and a flat-topped wall head; the spacing here is reconstructed at about 2.6 m. The sheet's small projection on the range's north wall (about 1.6 m out, 4.5 m long) is not built: no picture shows that side.

sash_by_storey.note: The bay's windows through the T-2541 camera on the 1888 plate (data/reference_views/coleman_ames_house_1811_prairie/inland_architect_plate.json): ground floor sills 2.04 m and heads 4.26 m over grade, first floor 5.46-7.57 m, about 1.05 m wide. The third storey's lights are the wall gable's (T-2542).

basement_lights.note: Area lights in the strip north of the bay; the bay's own basement lights are the grilled pair above.

roof_covering.note: The plate shows slate on every roof; Pennsylvania slate is the district's.

chimneys.note: The plate's tall stack at the junction of the front block and the brick range on the south side, and one on the north wall, reconstructed; T-2542 carried them up past the steepened ridge with it. Their corbelled caps and the range's second stack (the plate's, x about 545 px) stay open on the match record.

rainwater.note: No gutters yet: a K01 gable roof hangs none (T-2459). The plate's two downpipes on the front (at the bay's south return and the entrance block's south corner) are open on the match record.

window_kit.note: The district's two-over-two sash; the plate's sash is too small to count lights.

entrance_kit.note: The plate's deep round arch on clustered columns, its springing about 3.3 m and its extrados about 4.5 m over grade through the T-2541 camera on the 1888 plate (data/reference_views/coleman_ames_house_1811_prairie/inland_architect_plate.json), read on K07's deep-arched double door. The porch's depth, the columns and the stair's scrolled cheek walls are the finishing ticket's (T-1892).

gable_roof.note: The ridge at half the front block's depth, so the two slopes fall at the same pitch to the one wall head; the side walls carried up as coped parapets (K01's 'north' is the street's south end: the brick gable the plate and the Chicagology print show rising to the tall stack, a smooth coped rake, not crow-stepped).

dormer.note: T-2542: the north bay's STONE GABLE, read through the T-2541 camera on the 1888 plate (data/reference_views/coleman_ames_house_1811_prairie/inland_architect_plate.json), built as K01's wall gable (T-2428) on the street wall's plane over the bay, behind the balcony on its deck: centred on the bay (v 3.6); its rake's foot at about 10.2 m and its apex at about 13.2 m with a finial (x 192 px), so a face standing 1.95 m over the 9.14 m eave datum, 3.0 m across and pitched 55 degrees: its pediment's cornice at about 10.1-10.3 m and its apex at about 13.1 m; the third storey's three lights between their colonnettes, about 9.0-9.9 m and about 0.45 m wide on the plate, built at the wall gable's narrowest sash (0.5 m) 1.05 m apart, at T-2541's centres, 9.39-10.29 m (0.4 m high: a wall gable's face stands on the eave datum and its lights 0.25 m over it); a pinnacle either side at the bay's corners (x about 120 and 285 px, 3.7 m apart) rising to about 12 m under a pyramid. Reconstructed: the face's 3.0 m width (the plate's rake runs past the pinnacles' inner faces; K01 keeps each shaft clear of the face's cornice return), the pinnacles' square plan and pyramid tops (the plate's are carved and scaled), the panel, the lights' sash, and the voussoirs over flat heads where the plate shows plain lintels under the gable's great arched recess with its three small round-arched lights, which stays open on the match record for T-1892 (L-k01-1811-ames-front-2541).

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B; section2B brick with stone front dwelling (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1841 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: "Residence of Miner T. Ames, Chicago. Cobb & Frost, Architects." Photographic plate. The Inland Architect and News Record, vol. XII, no. 3 (October 1888), plate section ('Our Illustrations').
what_it_supplies: the street front's composition: the north bay, the entrance block, the oriel, their storey lines and openings, read at the scale the 1911 sheet's width gives the front
the south flank's storeys and that it is brick
the roof forms seen from the street: the gable over the bay, the pyramid over the oriel, the main roof behind, two stacks
what_it_does_not_supply: the north flank, the rear and the plan behind the front: the 1911 Sanborn sheet 28 supplies the plan
dimensions: no scale is printed; lengths come from the 1911 sheet

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 28.
what_it_supplies: The water's edge beside the Illinois Central from about 40 m north of 18th Street to about 80 m south of it, and the easternmost track on to the paper's edge, as of 1911
The 1800 Prairie lot and the Glessner House footprint (stone, courtyard plan) as of 1911, and every Prairie- and Calumet-facing footprint from 18th to 20th Street
Its own printed Scale of Feet
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-2541 (piece 1 of T-1891) refines the district draft (T-2330) in place under the same id from the Inland Architect plate of October 1888, 'Residence of Miner T. Ames, Chicago. Cobb & Frost, Architects.' (inland_architect_1888_10_ames_residence), read against the 1911 Sanborn sheet 28, which controls the plan. The draft's 7.25 m box (the largest rectangle its fit found inside the trace) becomes the sheet's own plan: a front block 10.4 m along the street and 7.57 m deep on K01 with a K02 rock-faced brown-stone front, its north bay standing 1.0 m proud on K08 and its corbelled oriel over the entrance arch, and behind it the 8.4 m brick range of three storeys and the two-storey rear section on K01's rear wings, 18.4 m back. The camera is solved into data/reference_views/coleman_ames_house_1811_prairie/inland_architect_plate.json; what the plate still shows differently is on its match record, and the roofs (the bay's gable, the oriel's pyramid) are T-2542's. docs/RESEARCH/k01-1811-ames-2541/README.md.
